reading: GRÜN · §64 — PG-14's fixed point: does frameWithBodies converge in its two passes, and does the frame it returns contain the bodies?
scope: arithmetic on committed constants, the committed layout spec and layout-golden-vectors-v1.1.json. No render, no server, no build, no browser, no credential.

model.map: half_{n+1} = max(half_n, max_b[|offset_b| + A_b · k_n]) with k_n = 2·half_n/drawnPx — monotone non-decreasing and affine in half
model.gradient: g = 2·A_max/drawnPx; a fixed point exists iff g < 1, and the iteration then converges geometrically at rate g
model.dominantTerm: `side` carries title.length · CHAR_EM · font / 2 with font = TEXT_MIN_PX · k · FLOOR_HEADROOM, so A grows LINEARLY with the role name's length. The golden vectors carry no titles, so length is swept.

divergenceIsNotALiveConcern.statement: Divergence appears only at title lengths of 64 characters and above, which is not a role name. So the 'no fixed point' branch is a robustness property of the iteration and NOT a defect anyone will meet; it is reported because the condition g < 1 is what makes the two-pass choice defensible at all, and because a future longer label walks toward it rather than falling off a cliff.

conclusion: PG-14's containment is zero-by-construction under A-G268, but the construction is a fixed-point iteration run exactly 2 times, and THAT is falsifiable without a mutant or a raster. It does not hold. A fixed point fails to exist in 66 of 440 swept cases, but only at title lengths 64/96/128 characters, which are not role names — so divergence is a robustness note, not a live defect, and it is not the finding. THE FINDING: the committed 2 passes do not reach the fixed point in 284 of 440 cases. The frame is emitted with a k computed from the PREVIOUS iterate, while the bodies are then drawn at the FINAL k, so the label's extent exceeds the frame that was sized for it. At an 8-character name the shortfall is sub-pixel everywhere (worst 0.45 px) and cannot clip a glyph. At a SIXTEEN-character name — "Product Manager" is fifteen — it is observable on 4 of 11 layouts at the component's own 420 px minimum width, worst 1.59 px on LV02; at 24 characters, 7 of 11 layouts and 6.12 px, and still 3 of 11 at 1040 px. So PG-14 is met at short names, and clipped at ordinary ones on a narrow window. The remedy is not a mutant and not a bigger constant: the loop has a convergence criterion available to it — iterate until `half` stops moving, which the sweep shows takes 1 pass at short names and up to 201 at the stress tail — and the choice of 2 is nowhere recorded as a decision. Changing it is a product delta and belongs to whoever owns the frame; this limb only establishes that two is a number rather than a proof, which is what GELB's §64 asked. What this does NOT say: nothing here is a measurement of a rendered frame. It is the product's own arithmetic run to more passes than the product runs it, which is why it needs no raster and no credential — and why it can be checked by anyone against the same two files.
